headline: Hollywood IS vertical. Netflix + Amazon + Disney confirmed the trifecta this fortnight. LA in 6 days — the conversations just changed.
whatChanged: This run covers the week of May 25, picking up where the May 23 brief left off. The defining development: the three largest US streaming companies all now have vertical video infrastructure. Netflix launched 'Clips' on April 30 in 9 markets, Amazon Prime Video launched its 'Clips' vertical feed on May 8, and Disney+ has been running vertical ('Locker Diaries') since February. Industry observers confirmed in the week of May 4-10 that vertical is no longer an experiment — it is standard premium-streaming infrastructure. This is bigger than the Peacock licensing deal from last week, because all three together is the entire Hollywood establishment. Tim's LA meetings (Jun 1-4) are now set against this backdrop. Every Microdrama-in-a-Box B2B conversation now has three additional proof points from the world's largest streamers. Two critical awards corrections: (1) StreamTV Awards — finalists announced May 12, the 2026 window is closed; the Jun 15 deadline in state was incorrect. (2) Campaign Asia 40 Under 40 — actual deadline was April 17, 2026 (not June 30); window is closed. MARKETING-INTERACTIVE Marketing Excellence Awards SG deadline corrected to June 12 (was listed as June 5) — 17 days out, still actionable. New intelligence this run: Issa Rae's 'Screen Time' on PineDrama hit 100M views (prestige Hollywood creator formally in microdrama); Marc Jacobs launched a luxury microdrama with Rachel Sennott (brand spectrum now spans FMCG to luxury fashion — seven confirmed brands); Park Min-Kyu (Single's Inferno, Netflix) cast in FlareFlow original 'One Year Love' (Vertical 2.0 casting); LA Vertical Drama Market held second edition May 7-10 at FAB Factory Hollywood with Apollo Awards (IAVA Gala — new award category for tracking); 'Clearly me' second AI consent violation in Chinese microdrama production (Category 22 — NEM prep).
